HRA Analysis: OVERVIEW:MISS ADDI (4) brings one of the strongest profiles of the program, with a strong record at this track and distance range, and comes off some first-rate form, including a win here two back when able to lead, with strong placings around that, including at Melton. There’s speed inside here, but the smaller field should allow her to map favourably and produce solid final sectionals, which she’s consistently been doing this time in. MASTER LOUEY (1) looks the main danger from the soft pole draw, with Herbertson aboard and the likelihood he will get his chance along the sprint lane after doing little work, trailing the speed as he’s done recently at this track. It all depends on the tempo and the momentum he gets into the straight as to whether he can run down the top pick. HILTONS SPIRIT (2) deserves respect based on current form, which has seen him win 3 from 10 this season, along with some solid recent sectionals last start at Melton. This is another strong race, but his soft map has him in the mix. KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3) is an interesting runner returning to VIC and his former stable, and did perform well earlier in the year. He has early gate speed and will no doubt look to be on the front end; just prefer to see him against this line-up. WOTDIDUSAAY (6) caused a big upset at Echuca and deserves consideration on that effort; this draw makes things a little tricky, however. BACK: MISS ADDI (4) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:MISS ADDI (4), MASTER LOUEY (1), HILTONS SPIRIT (2), KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3)

OVERVIEW:CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7) has been very honest, being runner-up in 4 of 6 attempts and racing well at this track. He got a good run and bumped into a handy one last time and just couldn’t match those sectionals when 2nd, while his runs prior were good, often from tricky draws. No favours with his marble again, but I fancy this is one of his most winnable opportunities. TOMBEUR (5) creates interest as a first starter off a trial win in slow time recently, and that was his first outing in a year. He’s from one of the state’s best stables, so monitor any strong market support. MEGALODON (8) is a well-named son of the mare Classic Shark and has shown promise in two career outings, finishing 3rd on both occasions. He goes from better draws to the back row but can get an economical peg run here and get his chance late. SIR KITT (1) is a 2yo who struck a very strong bunch of his own age on debut and now takes on more experienced types. He has a soft draw, and these shouldn’t put down the sectionals he faced last time, so he is open to improvement. BACK: CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7), TOMBEUR (5), MEGALODON (8), SIR KITT (1)

OVERVIEW:LIBERTY STAR DUST (5) is racing well, with a good win four back at Kilmore when given an ace drive, then went very close to winning at Geelong two back. Around those efforts, he was racing against the elite of his age group in the Vicbred Series. He’s only had the one start at Cranbourne for a win, and although he’ll need luck from the draw, he is a strong winning hope. CYCLONE JENNI (7) did a really nice job in winning from an awkward draw at this track four back and has been a little out of her depth class-wise since in the Vicbred. The draw is very tricky here but she deserves respect based on what she’s capable of. STORM VENDETTA (1) looks to get a very cosy run from the inside draw and has been racing well in his three runs for the new stable. He meets a few handy ones but must be included in exotics. HEZ HARRYWHO (2) finds a good draw and distance here to buck the trend of form he’s been in. That was the case four back when he found the front over the mile and wasn’t for catching at Kilmore. Look for a big bounce back on those key form indicators. FARROH JOE (3) is a 2yo taking on the older horses here and has run well in similar circumstances before, albeit in slightly easier company. He placed 2nd in his heat and 7th in the final of the Vicbred Series. WEONA OUR RIGHTS (4) is going okay, with his only failure to place this season coming when he drew wide in a Vicbred heat. He’s in the mix with the right run. SELECTIONS:LIBERTY STAR DUST (5), CYCLONE JENNI (7), STORM VENDETTA (1), HEZ HARRYWHO (2)

OVERVIEW: A good-quality race with a mix of 2 and 3yos, with the younger pair of LETITRIDELUV (2) and filly TWIGSTAR (3) looking the standout options. It’s agonising to make a definitive call between two horses who are racing so well at this level, but I must lean to TWIGSTAR (3) based on her excellent debut where she settled back in the field and ran away from them over the short trip. She now has a more favourable draw to press forward over the longer trip and potentially look for the lead. She’s already proven she can run time and, with natural improvement, will be very hard to catch. LETITRIDELUV (2) already has a decent scalp in his career in winning his maiden, then has acquitted himself very well against the elite of his age group in the Vicbred Series. He didn’t draw well in any of those races, and this favourable marble guarantees a positive map and every chance to win again; it’s just whether he’s capable of running times comparable to what the top pick did on debut. Would be surprised if that isn’t the quinella, with much of the remainder having claims at the minor end. BROADWAY OBSESSION (9) may be next best based on a strong SP profile and a solid place strike rate, with SWEET LADY LOU (8) and CALIFORNIA COOL (1) both benefiting from being on the peg line in what should be a strong last half. BACK: TWIGSTAR (3) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:TWIGSTAR (3), LETITRIDELUV (2), BROADWAY OBSESSION (9), SWEET LADY LOU (8)

OVERVIEW: Tricky race, being a standing start over the long distance for trotters and not presenting with the most reliable form under the conditions. EMWALLEN (3) has the most upside, being a lightly raced 5yo, winning 4 from 12 including two solid wins when able to lead all the way recently. This is his first crack under standing-start conditions, which is a slight concern considering some of his rivals love the tapes, but if you’re willing to take the risk, his ability can carry him a long way. MAESTRO (8) ticks a few boxes, being the most reliable and adept under standing-start conditions, a country cup winner under similar conditions and securing the services of Chris Alford. He’s a horse who seems to keep coming under slogging conditions, so he can overcome the back mark here. AVANT GUARD (7) will appreciate facing this sort of quality, having raced better types his past few. He was a winner in similar class four back but under mobile conditions. He’s yet to win from the tapes, but this is his best chance. EL CONQUEROR (5) likes the stand and longer trips and brings a favourable SP profile considering the opposition here. He doesn’t win out of turn, but his manners and the opportunity to get in front of some key rivals hold him in good stead. There’s a host of others worth considering, such as SOVEREIGN TIGER (6), who likes this track and is a last-start winner in easier company, and NEPHEW OF SONOKO (9), who, although he prefers mobile conditions, strikes the easiest race he’s faced in a while. SELECTIONS: EMWALLEN (3), MAESTRO (8), AVANT GUARD (7), EL CONQUEROR (5)

OVERVIEW: JUSTLIKEDAVE (7) was able to lead from this draw two back over the shorter trip and bolted in, winning by 18m and running fast time. He ran 2nd last start when a very short-priced favourite, but the run was still good after over-racing back in the field. His record over anything longer than the sprint journey is a concern, but his best form is hard to ignore. ROBLEN RANGER (2) could be a good roughie here, 2nd up from a break after doing plenty of work fresh. He has good speed to utilise this inside draw and map well. He can give cheek at a price and goes in the Quaddie for sure, no matter the odds. ROBLEN DEMON (5) is his stablemate and has been in good form this preparation, sitting tough and winning here two back. The map may be a little tricky but he can strike with the right run. The back-row runners BONA KHAN (8) and ALTA BAYAMO (9) can be very hard to catch, particularly from back-row draws, but they are worth keeping safe with the extra distance should those at the top end overcook things. BACK: ROBLEN RANGER (2) – 0.5 units (win) 1.5 units (place) SELECTIONS: JUSTLIKEDAVE (7), ROBLEN RANGER (2), ROBLEN DEMON (5), BONA KHAN (8)

OVERVIEW:SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) has the advantage of the concession to use a coveted pole draw and his good gate speed to get a comfortable lead over the short trip. He’s run well in his two runs with recent G1-winning driver Blake Pace aboard, and if he can tap the brakes in the middle section and get a lungful of air for the finish, he will be hard to run down. REASON TO LOVE (8) can catch his cover on the peg line and didn’t have much luck last time from a similar position. He can be an improver from the map and should be included in all multiples. CHASING THE WIND (9) has been popular with punters the past couple with Alford aboard, and having to do no work and come with one run here may suit depending on the tempo. ROCKNROLL RAMBO (10) is threatening to win, placing at his last four starts, but he goes to the back-row draw over the short trip, which hurts his chances. However, the closing sectionals shouldn’t be overly quick for him to make up ground late. DELTA STARZ (5) had a flat tyre last time and can improve based on his win four back, while it’s hard to know what to make of POWERLINC (6), but he is worth throwing in the wider Quaddie should you want to be safe. BACK: SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: SIR CANDY CLOUD (1), REASON TO LOVE (8), CHASING THE WIND (9), ROCKNROLL RAMBO (10)

OVERVIEW: PICKLE IT (5) looks the starting point here in a very even race where map and conditions will play a major part. This horse is a very quick beginner, relishes the mile and has a strong record at the track of 29:4-4-8. He’s probably been run off his legs with the times put down his past few, but those times are unlikely here, so he can hold on with the right tempo. OHHEMJAY CRESCO (1) is a one-batter who will be doing his best to hunt up from the pole, but he proved last start at Wagga that when he can roll along, he’s hard to get past. There are several horses that are map-dependent but are going well enough to include: GOZO MAJOR (4), DOT BALL (6), QUICK CRUNCH (7), FINAL BOW (8) and TOPHUT JOHNY (9). If things worked out, a win by any of them wouldn’t surprise at all. Maybe throw them all in the Quaddie if you want to go wide. SELECTIONS:PICKLE IT (5), OHHEMJAY CRESCO (1), QUICK CRUNCH (7), TOPHUT JOHNY (9)

OVERVIEW:FORTY LOVE (5) was heavily supported and ran a great race after working forward to find the lead in the early stages when a narrow second behind Fighter Command at Melton last week. He had no luck when sixth in the Super Series Final prior and he should prove very hard to beat under these conditions. OPERATIVE LINE (6) will also appreciate a drop back in class from his efforts at Metropolitan free for all level and should improve on his numerical form. He won the Stampede at Melton back in May. HOT DEAL (7) settled down last in a slowly run race and tried to sustain a long run out wide on the track when a game third behind My Ultimate Jimmy at Mildura on Wednesday. He is a versatile pacer and should run his usual honest race. RUFF NUT (2) and MADRIGAL (3) are both racing well enough to be worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: FORTY LOVE (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: FORTY LOVE (5), OPERATIVE LINE (6), HOT DEAL (7), MADRIGAL (3)

OVERVIEW:TAURAS (6) was resuming since July when he was without cover early, got in behind the leader at the 1300m and tried hard for a distant second behind Gaelic Lady at Terang. He should benefit from that performance and he was going nicely at the trials prior so he is capable of going one better. COLLEAGUES (5) has been placed in both of his efforts since coming from Queensland. He gained a nice trail and was going to run a clear second before breaking stride at the 150m at his latest Charlton third and he will prove hard to beat if he delivers a fool proof display. VIXAN (4) competed in a couple of Super Series events against much stronger opposition prior to a sixth at Terang, where she made several errors. She is better than her form reads and is a possible improver. DRESSEDUPINTHECITY (1) was caught without cover early, restrained to be fifth on the markers and battled on fairly well for fourth last outing. She is a maiden from 51 starts but she could fill a place from the pole position. SELECTIONS: TAURAS (6), COLLEAGUES (5), VIXAN (4), DRESSEDUPINTHECITY (1)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG HUSTLER (7) backed up several smart trial performances with a big victory over Dispersion at Terang, where he pushed forward to find the lead and completely dominated his rivals in handy time. He is widely drawn but appears to have a promising future and should prove hard to beat again. BAD GRANDMA (2) is a debutante for trainer Andy Gath, which scored nicely at a Melton trial on Tuesday afternoon. She is related to three winners and showed enough ability at her latest trial to warrant consideration. LOUS MAMBO (4) is a juvenile gelding that hasn’t raced since a victory in a fast mile of 1.56.5 at Charlton in May. He hasn’t been to the trials but will give a forward showing if he is somewhere near his peak form. BRIDWOOD MAISEY (9) was safely held at a recent Melton trial performance but she did make it through to the Breeders Crown Final last season so she cannot be left out of calculations. SELECTIONS: KEAYANG HUSTLER (7), BAD GRANDMA (2), LOUS MAMBO (4), BRIDWOOD MAISEY (9)

OVERVIEW: SKADI (3) began quickly to find the lead and was able to score comfortably when resuming at Swan Hill. She is a good chance of finding the lead again here and she did well after parking on the outside of the leader throughout at her latest third so she is capable of returning to winning form. MISSMALACHITE (6) progressed forward from a similar wide draw to race without cover when a brave second behind Doctor Go Joh at Terang on Monday night. This race is no harder and she should give another bold showing. DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1) finished a close up fourth in the race won by Doctor Go Joh and should receive every chance from the pole position. He has had a few chances since his latest victory but he is not without a winning hope under these conditions. ESPERANZA (4) led out then took cover and used the sprint lane when a close second behind Major Lincoln at Stawell. He won at Kilmore three starts ago and is one of the leading chances again. BACK: SKADI (3) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: SKADI (3), MISSMALACHITE (6), DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1), ESPERANZA (4)

OVERVIEW:CONNIES PRESIDENT (8) galloped away from the standing start and lost his chance at Charlton last outing but he was a runaway winner over BETSY ANNE (1) prior and he is drawn to gain an economical trip. BETSY ANNE (1) led out then took cover when third behind Money Talks at Kilmore last outing. She is a fast beginner and performs best over the sprint distance so she has the conditions to suit. I AM SKYE CHIOLA (10) competed against stronger opposition in a Super Series event last outing and finished midfield. She is a tough type and scored at Ballarat on August 26 so she is worth an investment. LOVE WHO (4) finished quickly via the sprint lane when a game second behind Rastamon at Maryborough last outing. He is racing well and looms as one of the leading chances again. SELECTIONS: CONNIES PRESIDENT (8), BETSY ANNE (1), I AM SKYE CHIOLA (10), LOVE WHO (4)

OVERVIEW:YANKEE RAIN (6) was heavily supported and shot to the lead shortly after the start when she led throughout at Terang last week. That was her best performance of the season and a repeat effort will see her go close to winning again. TORQUE IN HEAVEN (9) was very wide on the home turn and finished off fast for second behind YANKEE RAIN (6) at Terang. He won at his two attempts prior and is capable of turning the tables with normal luck in running. MONSIEUR FLAMEL (7) is a fast beginner and should be competitive from the wide draw. He commenced from the inside of the second line, was shuffled back on the markers and stormed home late when an unlucky second behind Foregone Conclusion at Kilmore last time out. MEGAWATTS (5) came from a rearward position when second behind Krissy in fast time at Shepparton last outing and is racing well enough to figure in the finish. SELECTIONS: YANKEE RAIN (6), TORQUE IN HEAVEN (9), MONSIEUR FLAMEL (7), MEGAWATTS (5)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY SNIPER (4) had little luck from poor barrier draws during the Super Series then followed with a big win at Terang, where he outstayed the handy performer Heavenly Gem. He is building up a handy strike rate and should prove hard to beat again. POSTERIZED (3) has been able to lead throughout in two recent victories and is drawn to lead again so he must be respected. He dashed home in a slick final half of 56.8 seconds when he held off Blazin By at his latest victory. GOLD IN PARIS (9) won three races in succession prior to a second behind King Kasey in fast time at Stawell, where she parked on the outside of the leader throughout. She is racing in career best form and is one of the leading chances again. CALF PEN (1) faces a steep rise in class but he has returned to his peak form and has leading reinsman James Herbertson aboard so he cannot be dismissed. BACK: JILLIBY SNIPER (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: JILLIBY SNIPER (4), POSTERIZED (3), GOLD IN PARIS (9), CALF PEN (1)

OVERVIEW: FROSTY DROP (4) attempted to lead throughout and was gunned down on the line when second behind Yankee Mojoh in a slick mile rate of 1.54.1 at Melton last outing. She is a good chance of finding the lead again and is capable of going one better. JILLIBY ZUCCHINI (11) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off strongly for an unlucky second at Terang when resuming since December 2024. She would have benefited from the experience and looms as one of the leading chances. MAJOR ROY (9) raced without cover throughout in fast time when a brave second behind Themidnightexpress last outing. He hasn’t had much luck in three starts since resuming and he should be competitive again. FOREGONE CONCLUSION (7) has won five of his past seven starts and was able to find the lead from a similar wide draw at his latest victory. This is a race of more depth but he is worth thought again. SELECTIONS: FROSTY DROP (4), JILLIBY ZUCCHINI (11), MAJOR ROY (9), FOREGONE CONCLUSION (7)

OVERVIEW: DISPERSION (1) was held up for a run at a vital stage and stormed home for an eye-catching third behind Baystyle at Melton when on debut then chased hard for second behind Keayang Hustler last outing. He is a promising maiden and is ideally drawn so he must be considered as a winning chance. LAMBRO LOUELLA (3) finished fast from midfield when a big second in the Ladyship Stakes at Globe Derby. She delivered a top run last outing and should be competitive again. MYDEEPESTDESIRE (7) raced on the outside of the leader throughout and went down fighting when a brave second behind Like A Gazelle on debut. She should have derived benefit from the experience and is worth thought again. EZEE FORTITUDE (8) is a first starter for trainer Andy Gath, which finished off in a slick final quarter of 28.1 seconds to win a trial at Melton recently so she cannot be left out of calculations. BACK: DISPERSION (1) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: DISPERSION (1), LAMBRO LOUELLA (3), MYDEEPESTDESIRE (7), EZEE FORTITUDE (8)

JILLIBY BLISS (6) put together an impressive win at Globe Derby when she held on to defeat EMILY MEGAN by a head at Globe Derby. She will find the draw tough today but she looks the one to beat based off recent form. MAGICAL MADGE (1) galloped at a vital stage last week but she could easily lead today and run a strong race if she trots smoothly. REHAB LAD (2) and PLATINUMS SON (3) are also chances.

MAIN BEACH (5) was impressive in a much tougher race last start. Today is easier but he will still need some luck from a tricky draw on a tight track. If he can run like he did last start and pace smoothly he will be hard to beat. JUST MILZY (2), ULTIMATE SAFARI (8) and CLARENDEN ARCADIA (7) are also chances.

PARISIAN BANDIT (3) ran second behind DONT TELL ALICE last start after being three wide for the last lap. He finds a very winnable race today and is well drawn. He could possibly lead and if he leads will hard to catch. WELL WELL (6), BRUZER (5) and DASHING COWBOY (2) are also chances.

LOCHINVAR HAWK (1) was run down after nearly leading all of the way at Globe Derby last start. He is a good chance of leading again today and being hard to catch after that better run last start. MURRA LANE (4), BROBENAH GIRL (2) and MACHFREDDY (3) are also chances.

IMA DESTROYER (1) was very impressive last start when she equalised the track record at Globe Derby and defeated TAKEN BY WINE by 20.4 metres. Today will be tougher but she has the inside draw and she loves the mobile start. QUARTARARO (10), MAORI TATTOO (3) and NOTHING I WANT (2) are also chances.

EDGAR BROMAC (1) has put together some promising runs in the early stage of his career. He broke his maiden last start at Mildura. He has gate speed and is a chance of leading all of the way today. LORD MYRMECIA (5), LIGHTNING BLING (6) and WHENIMREADY (9) are also chances.

SRIRACHA (1) finds an easier race this week compared to his last start at Globe Derby. He will love gate one and he should have the speed to lead. He is a strong chance if he is at his best today. AMIRA MARIE (4), A MAJOR STARR (2) and FENG SHUI STAR (8) are also chances.

PERFECT PLAYGIRL (1) has put together some encouraging runs since joining the Pullicino stable. She should be able to hold the lead from gate one which is a big advantage on this track. NORMY (5) looks like a big danger after a very impressive win last start at Globe Derby. CLARENDEN SAKURA (3) and FLYIN TOMMY (2) are also chances. Although there are only four runners in this feature two-year-old race, it is full of quality. POGACAR (3) couldn't have been more impressive in his two starts to date and looks to have plenty of improvement left in him going forward while he is still learning to race. STOLEN ONE (4) is the only filly in the field and will be looking to chalk up four wins in a row, while also replicating her last-start victory where she narrowly defeated HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (2) in a two-year-old track-record time. Tactics will be interesting here, with HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (2) looking the likely leader, while the other two main fancies may play cat-and-mouse tactics to see who is first off the pegs and forced to lead them up down the back straight. OUR ROBS ROY (1) hasn't been far away behind the above runners throughout his career to date, but you would think he will need to improve to win this in what looks an intriguing affair. Selections:POGACAR (3), HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (2), STOLEN ONE (4), OUR ROBS ROY (1) Staking Strategy:POGACAR will have to step up again here and possibly have a tougher run, but he looks the type that will. 2 unit win – POGACAR (3).

The low-class race of the night is over the mile, where PARK LANE (5) should show his customary sharp gate speed and cross to the pegs. He will no doubt roll along and give them something to chase, as he did last start, albeit in average time for the mile. JAY MILLER (2) resumes from a let-up but put together some nice performances before going for a break and looks to get every chance on speed with cover from the nice draw. MIKI SANZ (3) and FEELINKINDALUCKY (4) should also look to push forward and find prominent positions to give themselves their best chances. ROSE NOIRE (7) will need them to go hard up front to be running home strongly, after it was virtually impossible for her to make ground last start in a fast mile rate from the back row. You would expect the back-row runners to be in a similar boat and will be hoping for a genuine tempo to give them the opportunity to run home into the placings. Selections:JAY MILLER (2), FEELINKINDALUCKY (4), PARK LANE (5), MIKI SANZ (3) Staking Strategy:JAY MILLER should find a nice spot on speed and be in the finish. 1 unit win – JAY MILLER (2).

ARDEN SEASCAPE (1) is going for three straight victories since arriving in the state and couldn't have been more impressive in her two starts to date. This is a fair step up in grade though, and there also looks to be plenty of gate speed drawn to her outside, something she hasn't really been asked to contend with of late, but looks like there is plenty when aksed off her New Zealand form. CENTURIAN MISS (2) was checked when she looked as though she was about to be right in the finish last start and draws a nice gate to sit on speed. It is hard to discount ATOMIC BLACK (3) form since arriving in the state for Charlie Castles, as he continues to step up in grade, and you would expect him to also push forward from the nice draw. ANOTHER NIEN (6) may have a crack over the first 50 metres in an attempt to find a forward position, while CUZZY BRO (5) may be driven more conservatively this week after showing okay gate speed in previous starts in Free-For-All company, where he was able to win, similar to DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (4). The back-row runners are the more seasoned campaigners of the field and will be relying on some good tempo early and throughout to allow them to run home strongly into the finish. Selections:ARDEN SEASCAPE (1), CENTURIAN MISS (2), ATOMIC BLACK (3), CUZZY BRO (5) taking Strategy:ARDEN SEASCAPE looks hard to beat, but CENTURIAN MISS for a place looks the bet of the race. 2 unit place – CENTURIAN MISS (2).

There should be some good speed on early here, with numerous front-row runners coming into the race in good form. WEONA EAGLE (2) will be looking to cross the polemarker CRAYONS TO PERFUME (1), with both horses possessing excellent gate speed and performing well of late. IDEN OLIVER (5) has got the job done in four of his past five starts, although this is a step up in grade and he draws an awkward gate, similar to ART HUNTSMAN (6), who also has to overcome a tricky draw. SHOOBEES SPIRIT (8) should get a nice soft run behind one of the fancies and could be the one at odds if the gaps come his way late. The remainder look as though they may be running for minor prize money unless they go silly up front, which could bring WILL HE PIKE (12) right into the race late, as he has been running home strongly of late. Selections:CRAYONS TO PERFUME (1), WEONA EAGLE (2), SHOOBEES SPIRIT (8), WILL HE PIKE (12) Staking Strategy:CRAYONS TO PERFUME looks the horse to beat from the pole and is the most progressive horse in the field. 2 unit win – CRAYONS TO PERFUME (1).

Another even field here where numerous runners with sharp gate speed are involved, including LETSGOBRO (2), OUR WILLOW (3) and SOHO TIGER LILY (4), who you would expect will all have a good crack at leading the event. PORT RUN MACHINE (5) is a handy three-year-old but draws an awkward gate here, so will need a good steer to get into the finish, although you can't doubt his class. The above runners look the main winning chances in the field, with the remainder most likely racing for minor cheques for their connections. QUETZALLI (8) could be the one at odds, with the three-year-old filly taking on the older horses and likely to receive a soft run, where she could be dangerous if the gaps come her way late. Selections:OUR WILLOW (3), LETSGOBRO (2), SOHO TIGER LILY (4), PORT RUN MACHINE (5) Staking Strategy:OUR WILLOW should get a nice spot on speed with cover and may be hard to hold out late. 2 unit win – OUR WILLOW (3)

The Show Cup for the Free-For-All horses is always a competitive affair over the middle-distance journey, which gives those off the front marks a distinct advantage. WATERMELON SUGAR (3) looks the best of the front-mark chances and would only need to replicate his handy third last start against similar horses to be right in the finish. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (6) will again no doubt put himself into the race after beginning well, as he usually does, and will look to tough it out. The 20-metre backmarkers in GO THE RED (7), BETTABLACK TIGER (8) and CUSTOM HARLEY (9) are clearly the class horses of the field and will be relying on a solid tempo throughout and a good beginning early. You would expect all three to be running home strongly, as usual. Selections:CUSTOM HARLEY (9), BETTABLACK TIGER (8), GO THE RED (7), WATERMELON SUGAR (3) Staking Strategy:CUSTOM HARLEY is the class horse of the field and, with some solid tempo on throughout and a nice cart into the race, he’ll be running home strongly late. 2 unit win – CUSTOM HARLEY (9).

The maidens will again compete to break their duck, where most have had more than their fair share of chances to break through throughout their careers. DIAMONDONTHEROCKS (6) would be expected to use his sharp gate speed in an attempt to be first to the pegs, even from the wide draw, as he has done at his past three starts, where he hasn't been far away from winning. LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (5) should also look to push forward and should be suited by the mile distance. VOODOO RANGER (4) is a 33-start maiden who loves running a place in these types of fields and will break through one day. He should find a nice position on speed from the draw. CRUNCHTHEGUN (9) and ARRIVAL TIME (10) will be relying on some good tempo up front to allow them to run home into the finish, with the latter looking the better of those chances. Selections:DIAMONDONTHEROCKS (6), ARRIVAL TIME (10), LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (5), VOODOO RANGER (4) Staking Strategy:ARRIVAL TIME should be able to come with one run this week and could be hard to hold out late. 2 unit win – ARRIVAL TIME (10).

A tough race to finish off the night in what looks an extremely even affair. KENYA (1) draws the front row for the first time in a long time and has been running strong races while doing plenty of work, finishing as the bridesmaid on numerous occasions of late. However, there looks to be some handy gate speed drawn to his outside in LIKEABLE ROGUE (2), ALBERIO (3) and OUR SWEET TRIXIE (4), so he may look to get off the pegs early if the opportunity presents and be put into the race where he races best, which should ensure a solid tempo throughout. CHEYS ANGEL (7) was super impressive first up for the new camp in fast time after enjoying a nice sit behind the leader, but draws awkwardly here. TALK IS CHEAP (9) and COOLANDCOLLECT (10) should get nice runs from their trailing back-row draws and can be right in the finish with enough speed on up front. Selections:KENYA (1), OUR SWEET TRIXIE (4), CHEYS ANGEL (7), LIKEABLE ROGUE (2) Staking Strategy:KENYA will be looking to make use of a rare nice front-row draw and should be hard to beat on speed. 1 unit win – KENYA (1). OVERVIEW:THE GOLDEN HOOK (3) is racing in outstanding form and should prove hard to beat from his good draw. He worked forward to find the lead and blitzed his rivals at Gawler then followed with a brave second behind Luvtobeuptome in the Mildura Guineas. GOOD BOOTS BINDI (8) went back to last from a wide draw and was making ground before running into a dead-end late when an unlucky fifth behind Royal Saxon at Mildura last outing. She finished a close second behind the smart pacer Lewielewis prior so she will take holding out in the run to the finish. CHEERS POVERTY (2) is a fast beginner and performs best when he is able to lead. He attempted to lead throughout when a close second behind Royal Saxon last outing. STARVIN MARVIN (1) will appreciate his best draw for some time and has claims along with MY ULTIMATE BILLY (9). BACK: THE GOLDEN HOOK (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE GOLDEN HOOK (3), GOOD BOOTS BINDI (8), CHEERS POVERTY (2), STARVIN MARVIN (1)

OVERVIEW: It is a very open race with many winning chances. FLAME BLASTER (1) is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern and won from behind the leader at Mildura on August 21 so he is worth an investment. POTTSY THE GURU (2) hasn’t raced since August 2025 but he put together three straight victories at the end of his last preparation and he wasn’t beaten by far at the trials on Wednesday. He should go well from his good draw. CARLISLE CRUISER (8) was shuffled back on the markers after commencing from the inside of the second line and ran home fairly well for fourth behind Calf Pen last outing. He is worth a ticket each way from his trailing draw. SHES POPPY (11) pushed forward to find the lead from a wide draw and won comfortably on Wednesday. She does perform best when she is close to the speed and being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage but she won well enough last week to warrant respect. SELECTIONS: FLAME BLASTER (1), POTTSY THE GURU (2), CARLISLE CRUISER (8), SHES POPPY (11)

OVERVIEW: MAJOR LINCOLN (8) is yet to miss a place in five starts at Mildura and should run a good race again. He raced without cover throughout when a brave third behind SUNSHINE WARRIOR (9) last outing and he should go close from his trailing draw. SUNSHINE WARRIOR (9) showed very good gate speed to lead, kicked well clear on the home turn and held on to win at Mildura last outing. He drops back to the second line now but this race is no harder so he must be considered as a winning chance again. PUNTO CALIENTE (6) has been finding the line strongly at his most recent performances and is worth thought again. He came from last at his latest eye-catching third behind Keilah. FLEUR BELLA (5) is a fast beginner and her chances will be enhanced if she is able to find the lead around the first turn. HESASTAR (7) was a winner against similar opposition at Mildura on September 18 and has claims with normal luck in running. BACK: MAJOR LINCOLN (8) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: MAJOR LINCOLN (8), SUNSHINE WARRIOR (9), PUNTO CALIENTE (6), FLEUR BELLA (5)

OVERVIEW: GETONTHEBUS (1) boasts reasonable trial form in South Australia and is perfectly drawn for her debut. Trainer Peter Bain boasts a good strike rate at Mildura and GETONTHEBUS (1) is related to the handy Mildura performer Avoca Blues so she is sure to be strongly fancied. FEEFIFOFUM (3) parked without cover throughout and raced greenly when a game third behind Edgar Bromac at his Mildura debut. He has ability and should keep improving with the benefit of racing. PHILS BOY (2) settled midfield and worked home fairly well for sixth behind Miss Adelia on debut. This race is easier and his trial form is respectable so he warrants respect. ELISSAS DELIGHT (9) and CRUEL MISTRESS (11) have place claims and if the emergency LIKE A LIBRARIAN (4) gains a start, she will be competitive. SELECTIONS: GETONTHEBUS (1), FEEFIFOFUM (3), PHILS BOY (2), ELISSAS DELIGHT (9)

OVERVIEW:TO THE NINES (1) left a trailing position to park without cover mid-race and battled on strongly for third behind Gunforhire in fast time at Melton then followed with a close up fourth behind Pick Up Elvis in a strong race. He has returned from a spell in outstanding form and should prove hard to beat from the pole position. PRIORITISE (7) gained a one out and one back trail, came out three horses wide from the 600m and sustained a strong run when second behind My Ultimate Vinny on Wednesday. He is awkwardly drawn but appears to be well placed against this line up and is one of the leading chances again. SANTA CASA BEACH (6) is much better than his form reads and is capable of improving on his numerical form. He was held up badly behind tiring runners and seemed to have plenty in reserve when an unlucky ninth behind Hot Deal last outing. KYORETSU (5) possesses early speed and continues to perform strongly at Mildura so he warrants consideration. BACK: TO THE NINES (1) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: TO THE NINES (1), PRIORITISE (7), SANTA CASA BEACH (6), KYORETSU (5)

OVERVIEW:RANKINE (5) was slow to begin then circled around the field to park without cover when a big winner of the Lordship Stakes at Globe Derby when on debut. He overcame a tough run and won with plenty in reserve first up so he appears to have a promising future. SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (4) has joined trainer Robert Nolan since his latest race track appearance back in May. He looked impressive at a recent Mildura trial victory and must be respected. BAZZAS LEGACY (2) set up a genuine tempo in the lead when third behind Bersagliere two starts ago then followed with a distant fourth in the Mildura Guineas. He is perfectly drawn and should give a forward showing. COME ON BILLEE (3) didn’t have much room in the straight when fourth behind MY ULTIMATE HENRY (6) at his latest effort and is a place hope from his good draw. BACK: RANKINE (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RANKINE (5), SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (4), BAZZAS LEGACY (2), COME ON BILLEE (3)

OVERVIEW: ACCELERE (1) led throughout to win over ROJENBYE (5) on September 11 then followed with a third behind Caulonia Terror. He is drawn to lead again and should continue to build on his consistent form line. CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (7) gained a nice trail and battled on fairly well for third behind My Ultimate Henry last outing. He has the perfect trailing draw behind the likely leader and should run a good race again. THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (3) settled in the second half of the field and attempted to sustain a long run from the 700m when third behind Neds Beach last outing. He is better drawn for this assignment and is worth a ticket each way. ROJENBYE (5) was hitting the line strongly at his latest fourth. He has returned to form recently and should be finding the line nicely again. SNEAKY PHILTRA (2) and KEAYANG CRIPPA (6) both have claims in an open race to end the program. SELECTIONS: ACCELERE (1), CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (7), THE DEVIL ROLLS ON (3), ROJENBYE (5)

OVERVIEW:MISTER JIMARINGLE (1) ticks a few boxes to bounce back to winning form here. He strikes well over this distance and has a decent strike rate at this track, but his winning chances improve dramatically when he’s able to race on speed and dictate. Herbertson will no doubt use the draw to his advantage, with the map not working out last time when he was untested to the line. He finds a suitable grade compared with what he’s been opposed to and looks hard to beat. ROM BARO (10) is a 3yo who impressed last week at this track, winning in good time after leading all the way, dropping back out of the Vicbred Series. He goes to the back row now but deserves respect again. MAMMALS REASON (11) has a strong Shepparton profile, winning 4 from 8 here this season, all for the new stable. She goes to the back row, which makes things tougher, but her form is hard to ignore. IM DUSTEE (9) should be fitter now third up, and he hasn’t had much go his way in his two runs back, forced to sit outside the speed last time and settling too far back prior. Expect improvement. There are a few chances at the minor end, with TA KALCHE (8) likely to get a soft run and ANIMADO (3), MADAM REACTOR (4), MAJOR ORION (5) and GINGER ELLA (6) all racing well; they just have tricky draws to overcome. BACK: MISTER JIMARINGLE (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:MISTER JIMARINGLE (1), ROM BARO (10), MAMMALS REASON (11), IM DUSTEE (9)

OVERVIEW:PARINI (4) finds a winnable race to break his maiden after showing some promise in his five career starts, where often he hasn’t found an ideal set-up. He had nothing go his way first up, checked twice in running and crowded when making a run in the straight. He hasn’t shown gate speed to date, but this looks to be his most favourable opportunity to look for a forward spot and get every chance to break through. MAJOR FRIEND (11) has been racing well from better draws but goes from the pole to the outside of the back row. His form is better than most, so even though he’ll need luck, he warrants consideration. SON OF A BROAD (9) is first up from a break off a solid trial and, last preparation for the new stable, showed marked improvement, narrowly missing out twice when an odds-on favourite. Even though he will come on in fitness, the trailing draw and middle distance are in his favour. At the minor end, JUST MY LUCK (2) can improve as he’s likely to get a good trip, and it’s hard to know what to make of 2yo filly CARTIMANDUA (6), who was okay on debut but was quite poor when stepping up in grade since, while her trial wasn’t ideal. SLOWBURN (3) would also come into minor calculations with any scratchings. BACK: PARINI (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:PARINI (4), MAJOR FRIEND (11), SON OF A BROAD (9), JUST MY LUCK (2)

OVERVIEW:LUVERBOY (2) looks a really good value play, finally coming up with a good draw and looking to get a perfect map, likely behind the speed. Nearly half of his wins have come at this track, and when forced to be map-negative last week, he hit the line well when the race was over. The last time he got this likely map was in July when he won comfortably at Echuca from behind the speed. He’s a nice play on both totes. ELLEEGANT LANE (8) has really hit form this past month, winning 2 from 3, and at Melton no less, where she has run good time. Those wins have coincided with Liam Older, who seems to get on well with her, and although she’ll need luck from the draw, she deserves respect. TRYX VIXEN (4) drops well back in class from the Vicbred, but to be fair she didn’t make much of that last start when failing to beat one home, albeit in very quick time. If she can show better speed and find the front or race on speed, she can improve sharply; she must be kept safe. CRESCO THREEPEAT (9) is a tough type who races well at this track and grade. He beat home Ellegant Lane back in August. His chances depend on tempo. THERESHEWAS (5) and last-start winner YELLA (6) will need luck from the draw, but they should be considered for exotic plays. BACK: LUVERBOY (2) – 0.5 units (win) 1.5 units (place) SELECTIONS:LUVERBOY (2), ELLEEGANT LANE (8), TRYX VIXEN (4), CRESCO THREEPEAT (9)

OVERVIEW:ALCATRAZ GIRL (4) doesn’t bring strong numerical form, but her chances improve from what looks to be a nice map for her to roll forward and look for the top. She was a winner at this track and distance back in June when she found the lead and ran good time. Everything points to a form spike here based on those indicators, and she may represent value. WHERES WOOD WOOD (8) is just about racing in career-best form as a 9yo, winning 5 of her 15 races this season and placing another 8 times from 26 starts. She’s an exponent of the ratings system and often runs her best races when she drops back to this grade, looking well placed with the concessions, including that of Tasmyn Potter, who enjoys a good strike rate on her. KRAKEY (9) hasn’t won this season but is still racing okay. She was forced to do it tough outside the speed last week and looks to be an improver in this type of race. OLLY ODD POTTS (2) can be a little hard to catch, but she tends to run her best races in this class when she doesn’t do much work early and can come with one run. She must be kept safe. JOEYS HANGOVER (5) was a winner here last week when given every possible hope from a more favourable draw. Winning form is good form, however, so despite needing luck, he deserves to be considered again. BACK: ALCATRAZ GIRL (4) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS:ALCATRAZ GIRL (4), WHERES WOOD WOOD (8), KRAKEY (9), OLLY ODD POTTS (2)

OVERVIEW:AMADA VILLMA (5) has been very well supported in her past two runs and was narrowly beaten last time after being shuffled back the start prior. She looks to get her chance to lead again over the short trip here, and although she’s a 20-start maiden, with Herbertson sticking she gets a great chance to break through. EAGLEYE (9) has mixed her form in three runs for the new stable, but it’s a stable worth respecting, particularly at this level. Her run two back suggested she could go on with it, so if she brings that effort, she’s in the mix. BETTOR DOO (3) was fair here last week after having every chance, but that was a harder race than he faces here. This is only his 2nd run for the new stable, so he is open to further improvement. BERYLS BOOTS (6) has found form over the past month, placing at his past five runs. He’ll be dependent on the right cover, but he’s worth consideration. BACK: AMADA VILLMA (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: AMADA VILLMA (5), EAGLEYE (9), BETTOR DOO (3), BERYLS BOOTS (6)

OVERVIEW: Concession drivers race with a couple of different form lines. This is the lowest-confidence race of the night; it will come down to luck in running. Suggest field in the Quaddie. TOORAM DANNY (4) is one of those who brings a different lead-in, being fresh up off a decent trial at Echuca. He can be map-positive from this draw, and his only victory came when he led all the way over a similar trip. He has upside, whereas much of the opposition is exposed as far as form is concerned. OUR MYSTERY BET (6) comes out of a tougher race here last week after bringing some consistent form without winning. He sat parked and dropped out here last week, and on face value he was disappointing. He will likely sit outside the speed again, but on previous form he demands respect. ANGELIC ATTITUDE (7) is a tricky one to line up, racing in southern NSW with mixed results. The stable deserves respect, so she’s in the mix. LORIMERMAJOR (1) hasn’t won for a while but gets an economical run from the draw here. He got dragged back out of it last week, so he may be open to improvement. SELECTIONS: TOORAM DANNY (4), OUR MYSTERY BET (6), ANGELIC ATTITUDE (7), LORIMERMAJOR (1)

OVERVIEW: This is another concession drivers’ race, this time for the trotters. BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (4) brings what few others do in this race, and that’s current winning form. His victory two back was quite good when he was able to find the front and beat a similar-quality field to what he meets here. The stable thought enough of him to have a shot at the Vicbred last month, and the fact Riley Pace was a winner on him under normal conditions, against his junior rivals this time, appeals. PATNWILL (1) is up in grade, but he is a quick beginner suited by the mile. He was able to lead all the way from an inside draw at Melton five runs back, and a repeat of that will see him hard to catch. They appear to be the main winning hopes on form. COURAGES LAW (6) hasn’t been able to put it together this season but did show ability as a juvenile and can feature if he recaptures that. Stablemate AFRICAN GALA (7) went close to winning two back and did things wrong last time, but he appears to be racing a little better, while MONTANA MUSCLE (5) is the veteran of the field and has won three times this season, which holds her in good stead. BACK: BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (4) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (4), PATNWILL (1), MONTANA MUSCLE (5), AFRICAN GALA (7)

OVERVIEW:DEMBE (3) was a very good winner here last week in good time when he was able to map well and let down with a sprint to win easily. The driver/map combination is particularly pleasing here, with a proactive map position likely over the middle trip. He’s the one to beat again. CAPTAIN MOONLIGHT (5) is a big market watch here, being first up from NZ without a trial, and his NZ form is sound enough. Where he particularly stays under notice is with the astute trainer/driver combination at this level. RONNIE THE HAMMER (6) was first up here last week and performed well, considering the depth of the race and having to try to lead them up with fitness to come. He will be open to solid improvement. INTERPRETATION (4) ran 5th in the race that Dembe won last week but was drawn outside the back row and now draws to map closer. His form in Qld prior was okay, and he won’t be far away. SELECTIONS:DEMBE (3), CAPTAIN MOONLIGHT (5), RONNIE THE HAMMER (6), INTERPRETATION (4)

WANNABE ME (2) has very good gate speed and should be able to work to the lead in the early stages of this race from a good draw. She led two starts ago at Redcliffe and was just run down late there. SUZIE RHAYNE BOW (5) did things wrong on debut last time out and finds herself ODM as a result in this race. She had trialled up reasonably and with better manners this time she can play a part in the finish. HUSTLE AND HOLD (4) made a break last time out which took her out of play. She has good gate speed and should find a prominent position in this race. OLIVIA RHAYBE BOW (6) was running on well enough last time out into fourth behind Jewel Reason at Albion Park. She draws a touch awkwardly but can be running on late if the gaps appear at the right time. SELECTIONS: WANNABE ME (2), SUZIE RHAYNE BOW (5), HUSTLE AND HOLD (4), OLIVIA RHAYBE BOW (6) SUGGESTED BET: WANNABE ME (2) to win.

STONES (2) has good gate speed and should be able to find the front in the early stages of this race. He ran a good third last time out behind Doc Harvey at Albion Park in an effort that would likely see him hard to beat in this race. THE BLACK FOX (1) looks likely to get a good just behind the speed in this race from a good draw. He drew poorly last time out and wasn’t beaten far by Doolittle Doozzie there at Albion Park. GLENEAGLE HUNTER (6) should get a good run through in this race and should secure a good run behind the speed and with luck in running he looks hard to hold out late. He raced without cover last time out and battled on well there to finish a close up third. MY ULTIMATE LOUIE (7) didn’t have much luck last time out when held up at a crucial stage. He should settle close enough from a good draw and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: STONES (2), THE BLACK FOX (1), GLENEAGLE HUNTER (6), MY ULTIMATE LOUIE (7) SUGGESTED BET: STONES (2) to win.

SERENUS (7) took on a much stronger race two starts ago and wasn’t beaten too far by Carly Perez. She is having her first Marburg start for her career in this race and will just need to handle the track from a back row draw. GALVARINO (2) should have the gate speed to find the front in this race from a good draw. He scored a good win after racing on the pegs at Albion Park four starts ago in an effort that should see him hard to beat in this race. BOLD PERSONALITY (1) may be shuffled back a touch early in this race. She got shuffled back last time out in a race and was running on late behind Azor Ahai. WICKED MACK (9) secured a good run close to the speed last time out in what may have been a stronger race and was running on late into third behind Whata Good Feeling. SELECTIONS: SERENUS (7),GALVARINO (2), BOLD PERSONALITY (1), WICKED MACK (9) SUGGESTED BET: GALVARINO (2) to win.

MAN OF ACTION (4) has very good gate speed and may be able to zip across and lead. He hasn’t seemingly been at his absolute best in recent outings but does find a weaker race and could bounce back into some form. SAINT LOUIS BEAT (5) was running on late into third behind Deep Regret at Albion Park last time out. He draws poorly again and may need a few things to go his way in the run. SKIPPERS SWAN SONG (7) was well beaten last time out behind Smirks Lika a boss but wasn’t suited there racing off the speed in a race which became a dash home. With a more genuine tempo he can be running on late. KEAYANG TARA (9) was able to find the front last time out and was just run down late by Doc Harvey who had the perfect run behind the leader. She should get a good run off the speed and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: MAN OF ACTION (4), SAINT LOUIS BEAT (5), SKIPPERS SWAN SONG (7), KEAYANG TARA (9) SUGGESTED BET: MAN OF ACTION (4) to win.

OCTOBER RACKETEER (9) looks a clear standout on class in this race and will be hard to beat despite the outside back row draw. He raced without luck last time out and was running on late in a race taken out by Azor Ahai. YOGI (2) has good gate speed and may be able to zip across and lead early in this race which would likely see him hard to run down. He hasn’t started since late August which does look a query and he may need the run. MAJOR SLIP UP (6) draws awkwardly inside the back row and will need luck at the right time. Sat without cover last time out and battled on well for fifth behind Dipped In Silver. GRACENAVA (1) should settle close enough from a good draw in this race. She did things wrong from the stand start last time out and may be better suited back to the mobile in this race. SELECTIONS: OCTOBER RACKETEER (9), YOGI (2), MAJOR SLIP UP (6), GRACENAVA (1) SUGGESTED BET: OCTOBER RACKETEER (9) to win.

CHARLIE CHUCKLES (1) doesn’t have brilliant gate speed but does find a race which there doesn’t appear to be any brilliant beginners drawn on the front row which could allow him to drive through and lead. He got back in the run last time out and was making up good ground late behind Smirks Lika Boss. TAYLORS FOUR (6) should get a good run through behind the potential leader in the run. She isn’t quite racing at her absolute best but with an ideal draw in a race without huge depth she should get her chance. GOTTA DREAM (7) should get a good run behind the speed in this race. He secured a good run last time out at Marburg and battled on well for third behind Gidup Captain. He should run well again. COOL DUDE JOEY (5) returns from a spell in this race and draws poorly outside the front row. He will need a few things to go his way but is capable of figuring in a race of this nature. SELECTIONS: CHARLIE CHUCKLES (1), TAYLORS FOUR (6), GOTTA DREAM (7), COOL DUDE JOEY (5) SUGGESTED BET: CHARLIE CHUCKLES (1) to win.

BARRACUDA (2) should be able to work to the lead in the early stages of this race from a good draw. He led last time out at Albion Park over the 2138 and was able to hold off Camerina late who has since run well. BITE THE EAR MIKE (7) will be looking for four wins in a row in this race having impressed in recent outings. He was able to work to the lead last time out and proved too good for Major Crunch. BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) has good gate speed and can lead early before having options from there. He got back from a wide draw last time out and was running on late behind BARRCUDA (2) who he takes on again in this race. GREATGREAT BOULDER (6) appears to draw reasonably in this race to do no work early. He likely wasn’t suited last time out burning to lead and holding in a stronger race and could be better suited with a softer run. SELECTIONS: BARRACUDA (2), BITE THE EAR MIKE (7), BETTOR BE BOHDI (1), GREATGREAT BOULDER (6) SUGGESTED BET: BARRACUDA (2) to win.

SPLASHNDASH (1) should have the gate speed to lead early in this race. He sat without cover and battled on well there for sixth behind Studleigh Anne. He should be hard to beat. GLENLEDI BOY (6) looks likely to get a great run through in this race behind SPLASHNDASH (1). He will be relying on luck at the right time to get into the clear but is a horse suited by a soft trailing draw and should be hard to beat. DUAL CAM (4) sat without cover last time out and battled on well there to finish fourth behind One Last Roll. He may be left to do the work again in this race but looks capable. B MAC C (8) was running on strongly last time out behind stablemate Studleigh Anne. He should get a good run off the speed again in this race and can be running on late if the race is run to suit. SELECTIONS: SPLASHNDASH (1), GLENLEDI BOY (6), DUAL CAM (4), B MAC C (8) SUGGESTED BET: SPLASHNDASH (1) to win.
